clues.title: Concrete roads
text: If you're in Southeast Asia and see concrete roads, you're most likely in the Philippines, Thailand, or, much more rarely, Indonesia. If you're driving on the right side, it will be the Philippines, while driving on the left side indicates Thailand or Indonesia.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: South Mindanao car
text: In southern Mindanao, in the very South of the Philippines, there is some footage taken with a silver truck with a visible roof rack. Note that this is leftover, unculled old coverage that runs parallel to gen 4 images of the same locations, so you can still get the same roads with a different car.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Davao Occidental quad pancake insulator
text: If you see a quadruple pancake insulator on a pole top, you're going to be on the one road with coverage in Davao Occidental, along the coast, between approximately Don Marcelino and Bukid.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: East Samar double pancake insulator
text: Double pancake insulators are very rare, but most likely to be found along the coast of East Samar, from about the height of the island of Hilabaan all the way down to the southern tip.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Bohol thick insulator stem
text: The stems on which insulators sit at the top of poles is commonly thick or encased in a plastic tube that makes it appear much thicker than usual on the island of Bohol.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: North Luzon Chile poles
text: Chile poles can be frequently found in northern Luzon, especially Cagayan, but careful - they can also appear, if less commonly, in northern Negros!

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Mesh poles
text: Flimsy mesh poles are common in the province of Zamboanga Sibugay. They also, rarely, appear in other provinces, but even then you should be on Mindanao.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Northwest Leyte and Biliran extender insulators
text: Three ridges plus a long extender at the top to carry the wire are most commonly found in northwestern Leyte and northwestern Biliran.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Manila sausage insulator
text: This grey insulator with lots of small ridges that looks kind of solid is most common in and around Manila, but can rarely be found elsewhere.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Manila and Ilocos Norte Star Wars insulator
text: This type of insulator that looks like the buildings on Tatooine is most common in northern Luzon and in and around Manila.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Ilocos Norte and Biliran quad insulator
text: This cylinder with four distinct ridges is most common in Ilocos Norte, but can also be found in southern Biliran.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Octagonal metal poles
text: Octagonal metal poles are quite common in the Philippines.
NOTE: They can sometimes be found in Bangladesh and some parts of Malaysia as well.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: North Cebu yellow blocks
text: In northern Cebu, you will find gray concrete guard blocks with their edges or sides painted yellow. These are not the only guard blocks in the area, so don't discount northern Cebu if you see, for example, fully yellow concrete blocks or walls and blocks with diagonal black and yellow stripes.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Panay & Guimaras yellow backboards
text: On the islands of Panay and Guimaras (the little island next to Iloilo), electricity counters are frequently mounted on yellow backboards. These can be horizontal or vertical, metal or wood.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Palawan trike
text: The trikes on the island of Palawan are recognizable by their single wide front window. Many of them look as if they were cosplaying as cars, with emblems and everything.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Southern Quezon acne blocks
text: The southern peninsula of Quezon has these sloped concrete blocks with round spots made from small rocks that kind of look like a skin issue. Blocks in this style with straight edges are common throughout the country, and you can get slanted concrete blocks without the acne in other places as well, but the combination is exclusive to this area.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Guardrail: Bicol Adidas guardrails
text: In an area including Bicol, Catanduanes and Masbate, you will see guardrails marked with three black stripes. Careful: you can get more or fewer than three in other places as well, but if you see three, it is most likely going to be this area.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Quezon blue/red blocks
text: In a small area on the isthmus of Quezon province, you will find alternating red and blue guard blocks.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Trikes/Tuk-Tuks
text: Tuktuks and Trikes are an extremely common sight in the Philippines. In many areas, they are more common than cars.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Road line: Yellow and white lines
text: Center lines in the Philippines can be white or a (usually slightly orange-tinted) yellow. The combination of the two colors, which you can also often get, is not really a thing anywhere else in Southeast Asia and as such is a good indicator for the Philippines.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: Middle road lines in the Philippines can be either yellow or white, they can also be full white.
In particular, you will often see combined yellow and white middle lines, which is not common in any other East Asian country.
Yellow road lines commonly have a distinct orange tint.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Mayon Volcano
text: The Mayon Volcano is one of the tallest mountains in the Philippines and can be recognised by its almost perfect smooth cone shape. Beware that it will very often be covered in clouds.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Arayat Volcano
text: The Arayat Volcano can be recognised by being completely surrounded by flat agricultural fields.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Bohol Hills
text: On central Bohol you can find these distinct round grassy hills. The hills generally have dark brown soil beneath the grass, earning them the name of Chocolate Hills.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Northern Luzon
text: The forested mountain range in Northern Luzon is characterised by somewhat dry mountainsides and an abundance of pine trees. You may rarely come across a similar landscape on high-altitude roads in Mindanao.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

Thailand also has a lot of concrete roads.

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Northern Luzon Landscape
text: The forested mountain range in Northern Luzon is characterised by somewhat **dry mountainsides** and an abundance of **pine trees**. You may rarely come across a similar landscape on high-altitude roads in Mindanao.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Agriculture - Corn
text: While **corn** can be found in most of the country, it is most common on northern Luzon and on Mindanao.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Agriculture - Oil
text: The vast majority of **Oil** palm plantations are found on Mindanao.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Agriculture - Banana Plantations
text: **Banana** plantations are almost exclusively found in central and southern Mindanao.
NOTE: Wild growing banana plants can be found all over the country, so make sure what you are seeing is an actual plantation before guessing.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Agriculture - Sugarcane
text: The majority of **sugarcane** in the Philippines can be found on the islands of Negros and Panay.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Agriculture - Pineapple
text: **Pineapple** plantations are mostly found on Mindanao.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Moluccan Albizia
text: Moluccan albizia are trees with **light coloured trunks** and **pinnate leaves** near the top of the tree. They are mainly found on Mindanao and are especially common in the eastern and central regions of the island.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Architecture - Diamond Amakan
text: Houses built with amakan walls, a traditionally woven bamboo mat, with a **diamond pattern** are almost exclusively found in the southern half of the country.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Architecture - Diagonal Amakan
text: Houses built with amakan walls (referred to as Sawali in the north) with a **diagonally woven pattern** are mostly found on the island of Palawan, but can also be found throughout the northern half of the country.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Guardrail: Infrastructure - Black & Yellow Guardrail
text: In the Cordillera Administrative Region you can find **yellow and black** striped concrete guardrails.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Guardrail: Infrastructure - Bicol Stripes
text: White guardrails with **three recurring black stripes** are unique to the region of Bicol in southern Luzon.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Infrastructure - Indented Pole
text: Square concrete poles with an **indent** on both side, similar to the poles found in Chile, are mainly found north of Manila and in and around the city of Bacolod on the island of Negros.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Ladder Poletop
text: A poletop made up of two tall vertical metal bars having an L-shaped cross-section which are connected via several thin wires, making it resemble a ladder, is unique to Manila and the surrounding area.

NOTE: You may sometimes come across similar looking poletops, with square bars instead of L-shaped ones, throughout the entire country. They will however almost never have more than two connecting wires.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Infrastructure - Square Metal Mesh Poles
text: **Square metal mesh poles** are found on Mindanao, mainly on the Zamboanga peninsula.
NOTE: Most of the poles found outside of the Zamboanga peninsula are found along highways and have poletops with three hanging insulators.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Culture - Islam
text: While most of the Philippines is strongly christian, a region of western Mindanao is majority **muslim**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Culture - Mountain Dew Decorations

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vehicle - Kuliglig

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Bataan Death March
text: These large decorated white waystones, commemorating the Bataan Death March, can be seen along roads going from Mariveles and Bagac in the south to San Fernando in the north.
NOTE: The Bataan Death March continued from San Fernando to Capas by train, where a larger memorial has been built.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Palawan Highway
text: The highway going south from Puerto Princesa on Palawan can be characterised by being very wide, often featuring six lanes, while simultaneously having very little traffic.
Along the road you will usually see this double electrical wire, which can help confirm your guess.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Siquijor Lamp

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Culture - Roman Soldiers

clues.title: Architecture: Vehicle - Crown Roof Tuk-Tuk

clues.title: Pole: Square metal mesh poles
text: Square metal mesh poles are found on Mindanao, mainly on the Zamboanga peninsula.
NOTE: Most of the poles found outside of the Zamboanga peninsula are found along highways and have poletops with three hanging insulators.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: L-shaped cross section
text: A poletop made up of two tall vertical metal bars having an L-shaped cross-section which are connected via several thin wires, making it resemble a ladder, is unique to Manila and the surrounding area.

NOTE: You may sometimes come across similar looking poletops, with square bars instead of L-shaped ones, throughout the entire country. They will however almost never have more than two connecting wires.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: Philippines
text: Standard white licence plates with black text are used for passenger vehicles. You can also find many that are privately issued, which are recognizable due to their green tint, which is actually quite common to see.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Infrastructure - Trike - Zamboanga Peninsula
text: This trike shape is essentially the only variant seen on the entire Zamboanga Peninsula. What sticks out to me is the passenger window shape- it’s kind of like an airplane window. Other notable parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window.
It’s identifiable from the back as well from the singular window in the back, as well as the roof tilting, and the random bars on top.

A common variant is this one with a large window hanging over the driver’s side. You can tell it’s the same type of trike from the same shape of the passenger car- where it has the airplane window (even if it’s horizontal) and then the bit beneath it that’s completely vertical and flat, along with the roof tilting back.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - K-Waystone
text: These waystones with K and a number below show the distance related to Manila (or the max distances on specific islands)
This number can be used to narrow down guesses.
For example, certain islands cannot exceed the orange numbers on the image. As another example, Mindanao, and nowhere else, always has numbers above 1000.

clues.title: Architecture: Infrastructure - Trike - Zamboanga City
text: The Zamboanga Peninsula trike is recognizable through the passenger window shape (airplane window). Other notables parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window. Some cities have specific variants of this Trike:

This trike is a Zamboanga city trike- they have a flat roof, a white line separating the passenger and the driver’s side. There’s a little bumper thing jutting out from under the window, and there’s still the vertical bit underneath the passenger’s window. Zamboanga city specifically has these super colorful trikes.

This type of trike is still identifiable from the back due to the black cloth roof, the large window with the singular white line, and the back having a side window. These less colorful variants can be found Northeast of the main city.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
